record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.original_question: For a positive integer n, especially in the open range n >= 5 stated by the source, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of real numbers to be exactly the spectrum of an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer with n ≥ 5. A real n×n matrix A = (a_{ij}) is called (entrywise) nonnegative if a_{ij} ≥ 0 for all i, j. Given a multiset Λ = {λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n} of real numbers, Λ is said to be realizable as the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix if there exists an n×n entrywise nonnegative matrix A whose characteristic polynomial is ∏_{i=1}^n (x − λ_i), i.e., whose eigenvalues counted with multiplicity are exactly λ_1, …, λ_n.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the multiset Λ = {λ_1, …, λ_n} of real numbers for Λ to be realizable as the spectrum of some n×n entrywise nonnegative matrix.
artifact.status_search_result: The Real Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem (RNIEP) was solved by Loewy and London (1978) for n ∈ {3,4}. For n ≥ 5 it remains a longstanding open problem: only various sufficient conditions and partial results are known, and the problem has been shown to be NP-hard. No complete necessary and sufficient characterization is available.

status_evidence.claim: Complexity-theoretic obstruction; problem remains without explicit characterization.

status_evidence.title: A note on the real nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem
status_evidence.snippet: Updates on partial sufficient conditions for RNIEP.
status_evidence.claim: Only sufficient conditions are known for general n.
